answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with dawn audits: every epoch, a lottery picks random identities that must answer a fresh signed liveness challenge within minutes. One real operator passes easily, but an attacker running a grove of fakes must keep every socket alive, hold every key, and answer simultaneously across time zones - a coordination cost that grows per fake while revenue per fake stays flat. Pair this with a small refundable juniper deposit, forfeited on missed audits, and fake identities become inventory that costs rent instead of free entries.
